alt: Primary socialisation in the family, secondary socialisation beyond it, re-socialisation such as military training or prison, and inadequate socialisation shown by the Genie case and contested New Right claims.
caption: Isolation cases suggest much of “human nature” is learned.

alt: A grid of six agencies of socialisation, families, schools, peers, media, religions and the workplace, with their methods and points for analysis, plus formal versus informal and deliberate versus unintended methods.
caption: Link an agency to a method, then to a perspective.

alt: Mead’s stages from imitation through play and games to the generalised other, and Cooley’s looking-glass self, in which how we imagine others see us shapes how we see ourselves.
caption: For interactionists, the self is built through taking the role of others.

alt: A grid of functionalist, Marxist, feminist and interactionist views of socialisation: what is passed on, key evidence such as Parsons, Bowles and Gintis, Oakley, Sharpe and Mead, and a criticism of each.
caption: Each perspective reads the same process as consensus, ideology, patriarchy or negotiation.

alt: Bowles and Gintis’s correspondence principle: obedience to teachers, acceptance of school hierarchy and motivation by grades mirror obedience, hierarchy and wages at work. Willis’s lads resisted but still entered manual work.
caption: For Marxists, the hidden curriculum prepares obedient workers.
